title: Name appendix files {artifact-name}_{type}_{filename}

facts.note: Whether a file is an appendix (supporting file such as a mockup, diagram or spreadsheet owned by a planning artifact) is inferred from its role, not from its path; the source sets no location restriction, so appendix identity must be judged regardless of where the file is stored.

Non-exclusive heuristic only: a file under an appendix storage location (see planner.appendix.storage) is a strong signal it is an appendix, but appendices stored or referenced elsewhere are still in scope. The path is observable; appendix identity outside it is llm_judged.

Create/rename/edit of a file is observable from the diff; review of existing appendices is a task/phase fact; detecting that a plan, acceptance or doc references an appendix filename (new or existing) needs a reference observer or LLM judgement. For edit/review the rule fires when the appendix filename does not match the pattern (needs a filename-pattern observer).
Plans or docs that attach or cite supporting appendix files for any owning planning artifact (e.g. a wagon, WMBT, feature or component).

fires: Planner adds a new appendix file (e.g. mockup, diagram, spreadsheet) for an owning planning artifact, wherever it is stored.
Planner renames or moves an existing appendix file.
Planner edits or reviews an existing appendix whose filename does not match the pattern (e.g. editing overview.png in place), even without renaming or referencing it.
A plan, acceptance or doc references an appendix filename, whether the appendix is about to be created or already exists (including an existing misnamed appendix such as overview.png).
doesNotFire: Editing the content of an already correctly named appendix file without renaming or referencing it under another name.
Files that are not appendices (plans, wagon/WMBT/acceptance definitions, source code, tests), even if they sit near appendix files.
Choosing which appendix type applies (governed by planner.appendix.types) or where to store it (planner.appendix.storage).

given: A planning artifact (for example a wagon, WMBT, feature or component) has, or needs, a supporting appendix file, regardless of where that file is stored.
when: The planner creates, renames or references that appendix file, or edits or reviews an existing appendix whose filename does not follow the pattern.
then: Name the file {artifact-name}_{type}_{filename}: the owning artifact's name first, one of the six recognized appendix types second, a descriptive filename last, separated by underscores.
prefer: Use the owning artifact's exact name/id as the first segment (e.g. wagon slug, WMBT id like E023, feature slug, component name).
Take {type} only from the six recognized appendix types listed in planner.appendix.types (e.g. mockup, diagram, spreadsheet); look the list up there rather than guessing.
Make {filename} descriptive of the content (e.g. overview, sequence, tax-rules, states); hyphens are fine inside a segment.
When editing, reviewing or referencing an existing misnamed appendix, rename it to the pattern and update references to the new name.
avoid: Bare filenames missing the {artifact-name} and {type} segments (e.g. overview.png).
Hyphens instead of underscores as segment separators (e.g. checkout-flow-mockup-overview.png).
Inventing a {type} value outside the six recognized appendix types.
why: Encoding the owning artifact and appendix type in the filename ensures uniqueness, traceability back to the artifact, and clear type identification without opening the file.
evidence: Every appendix filename (created, renamed, edited, reviewed or referenced) splits on '_' into exactly three parts: artifact name, type, descriptive filename (+ extension).
The first part matches the name/id of an existing owning planning artifact (e.g. a wagon, WMBT, feature or component).
The second part is one of the six appendix types defined in planner.appendix.types.
verifier_detail: Pattern: {artifact-name}_{type}_{filename}; underscores are segment separators, hyphens may appear inside segments.

Positive examples: checkout-flow_mockup_overview.png (wagon); E023_diagram_sequence.svg (wmbt); payment-processing_spreadsheet_tax-rules.xlsx (feature); PaymentForm_mockup_states.png (component). The artifact-kind annotations are illustrative, not an exhaustive list of owning artifact kinds.
Negative examples: overview.png (missing {artifact-name} and {type} segments); checkout-flow-mockup-overview.png (uses hyphens instead of underscore separators).
Term id: naming_pattern. Rationale value: ensures uniqueness, traceability, and clear type identification.

Appendix identity is not determined by path: an appendix storage directory is a non-exclusive signal; apply the pattern to appendix files and appendix references anywhere, including existing misnamed appendices that are edited or reviewed.
